scenario: AITA for not wanting to attend my great aunt's funeral? | So today I came home from college (Britain, so American High School, I think). The second I walk through the door my mum tells me that her grandma's sister has died. "Your great aunt Wyn died and the funeral will probably be soon." My first thoughts were 'Who?' and 'Why is she telling me this?' I have actually never heard this name before or met this person besides the one time I found out today I had met her when I was still extremely young and unable to walk for myself. This turned into a slight argument as, for some reason, she wanted me to go this funeral, despite knowing I am a really awkward person at funeral's for people I've met more than once, let along a funeral for someone I've met only once and have no idea who is part of the family. The argument ends with her trying to guilt-trip me by outright just saying "Fine, I'll go on my own." in a really sulky way. Her only arguments for me going were that I'd be going out of 'respect' and support for her, despite that she has never once mentioned this great aunt to me even though she supposedly played a massive hand in raising her as my grandmother, and that it's one of the few times we'll see the much larger branch of the family where it's likely to be a few hundred of us, about 10 of which I have seen more than once but still at most 10 times, maybe not even that. To me, it would feel like gatecrashing the funeral for someone else's family and that, even though I am part of the family, no one would want me there since I do not know nor did I know the person who died. I don't know how much this takes precedence over everything else but it felt like it had to reiterated a lot - I have never met this person besides the one time she met me when I was either 1 or 2 years old and the name has never been mentioned to me before now, at least not to my recollection. So, AITA for not wanting to attend someone who is practically a stranger to me's wedding for the sole reason that she's family?

Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's morally acceptable for this person not to attend their great aunt's funeral. Let me break this down step by step.

First, the scenario is that the person is a college student in Britain, so they're probably around 18-22 years old. They come home from college and their mum tells them that their great aunt Wyn has died. The person has never heard of this name before and only met the great aunt once when they were extremely young, like 1 or 2 years old. So, they have no real connection to this person.

The mum wants the person to attend the funeral, but the person feels awkward at funerals, especially for people they don't know well. They argue about it, and the mum guilt-trips them by saying she'll go on her own. The mum's arguments are that the person should go out of respect and support, even though she's never mentioned the great aunt before. The person feels like they're being forced to attend a funeral for someone they don't know, and it feels like gatecrashing a family event.

The person is asking if they're AITA (Am I The Asshole) for not wanting to attend. So, the question is whether it's morally acceptable for them to refuse to go to the funeral.

I need to consider the moral aspects here. Is it wrong to not attend a funeral of a distant relative you've never met? Or is it understandable given the circumstances?

On one hand, funerals are about respecting the deceased and supporting the family. Even if you don't know the person, attending can show solidarity with the family. On the other hand, if the person has no emotional connection to the deceased and feels uncomfortable attending, is it wrong to prioritize their own feelings?

Also, the mum's approach seems manipulative, guilt-tripping the person into attending. That might affect the moral judgment as well.

I think it's important to balance respect for the family with the individual's feelings and comfort. If attending the funeral would cause significant distress, it might be more compassionate to not attend, especially if the person has no meaningful connection to the deceased.

Moreover, the mum has never mentioned the great aunt before, which makes the situation more confusing for the person. It's understandable that they feel disconnected and unsure about the importance of attending.

In conclusion, while attending funerals is generally seen as respectful, in this case, given the lack of connection and the person's discomfort, it might be morally acceptable to decline.
